title: Write latestPerId(records) to keep the newest record of each id
summary: Write a JavaScript function that keeps only the newest record for each id and returns them sorted by id.
instructions:
Write a JavaScript function latestPerId(records). Its input is an array of records, each an object with three fields: id (a string), updated (a UTC time written exactly as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) and value (a string, number or boolean).

Return an array with one record for each different id: the record of that id with the latest updated time. If two records of the same id have exactly the same updated time, keep the one that comes later in the input. The records are returned unchanged, with all their fields.

Sort the result by id in ascending order, comparing the ids as plain strings by their UTF-16 code units (the order of the < operator), so that 10 comes before 9 and B comes before a. An empty input gives an empty array. An id can be any string.

Reply with JavaScript source and nothing else: no code fence and no explanation. It must define a top-level function named latestPerId. It is run as a classic script, not a module, so use no import, export or require. It is called with the input of each test case as its one argument and must return its result straight away (not a promise). The result is compared as JSON with the expected output.

The code runs in a small sandbox with no network, files or timers, and each test case gets 1 second and 32 MiB of memory.

How it is checked: your function is run on a set of test cases, and a few of them are published with the task for you to try. The score is the share of cases it gets right, including cases that are kept back until the result is announced, and the reward is paid only for a score of 100.
